thesis: Ethereum is the asset the flows are leaving. ETH product inflows fell 73-96% in the week to 4 Sep while bitcoin funds took $986.9M, and ETH is still under $3,000 with a structural argument - L2s capturing the fee revenue that used to accrue to L1 - that price action is agreeing with. Momentum of +39.3% over three months is real, but RSI 52 and no breakout say the move has stalled. Hold, do not add.
bull_case: The three-month trend is intact and substantial: packet close 2,505.07 with close > SMA50 > SMA200 and 3m momentum +39.3%, and our position is marginally green. Institutional demand exists in size when it shows up - Tom Lee's Bitmine bought $131M of ETH on 31 Aug, the largest single purchase since June - and Bitwise's Matt Hougan named Ethereum in his tokenization basket (5 Sep). Analyst September targets cluster around $2,800 with a range of $2,334-$2,950, so the consensus band sits above spot.
bear_case: Three independent problems. Flows: ETH product inflows fell 73-96% in the week to 4 Sep, and Ethereum ETFs ended their winning streak on 3 Sep while bitcoin's continued. Structure: scaling moves activity to L2s, which cuts L1 fee revenue and the ETH burn, so adoption no longer mechanically accrues to the token - this is the argument that has kept ETH under $3,000 all year. Competition: Solana is taking developer and trading share, and Japan's Remixpoint dumped its ETH and XRP for a bitcoin-only treasury on 2 Sep. RSI 52 with no breakout is a stalled trend, not a base. Base rate from our own backtest (research/backtests/2026-09-06.md, 730 days, generated 2026-09-06): the crypto sleeve returned -6.4% with Sharpe -0.15, a 17% win rate over 75 trades and a -19.2% max drawdown, while us_stocks returned +7.6% (Sharpe 0.63) and au_stocks +3.7% (Sharpe 0.57) on the same rules. Trend-break exits alone lost 1,028 in crypto across 39 trades. This system has no demonstrated edge trading crypto momentum, and out-of-sample being +5.3% on a short window is not proof that it does. Every crypto conviction below is capped by that.
catalysts: Weekly ETH ETF flow prints - a return to positive would change the flow leg
Any L1 fee-capture change that reverses the L2 value-leakage argument
risks: ETH product inflows down 73-96% in the week to 4 Sep
L2 scaling structurally reducing L1 fee revenue and burn
Solana taking developer, RWA and trading share
Treasury holders rotating ETH into bitcoin-only mandates
Own backtest: negative expectancy for crypto momentum in this system
invalidation: Flips long on a daily close above 2,700 with two consecutive weeks of positive ETH ETF net inflows; the bear case confirms on a close below 2,334, the bottom of the analyst September range, which would also break the SMA50 structure.
